disclaimer: This is a structured decision analysis for a single asset. It is not legal, tax, or investment advice, and it is not a valuation appraisal. All deal-specific terms must be supplied by the principal; all market inputs are sourced on the Data & Sources page.

options.name: Sell now, before lease-term decay and while the market is liquid
options.mechanics: Market the asset now on the remaining term (target 2026-2027), accept the lease-term discount, and redeploy proceeds into a diversified or longer-WALT position via a 1031 exchange.
pros: Converts a single-tenant, single-city, single-tenant-credit risk into liquid capital at a known cap rate.
Removes R01, R07, R08, R09, R11 exposure immediately; removes R03 entirely.
Locks in today's pricing while Treasury yields are near the top of their 2026 range (S09) rather than waiting for further cap-rate expansion.
A 1031 exchange defers the federal gain if the 45/180-day rules are met (S24).
cons: Pays the lease-term discount now, i.e. sells the shortest WALT of the whole holding period.
Triggers Measure ULA and city transfer tax at 4.45% of price above $5.4M (S23).
Resets Proposition 13 base-year value for the buyer, which the buyer prices back into the cap rate (S20).
Gives up the option value of a below-market inherited base and of a renewal-driven re-rating.
Restarts the 1031 clock: replacement property must be identified in 45 days and acquired in 180 (S24).
options.best_if: You need liquidity or diversification, or your view is that cap rates keep expanding.

options.name: Hold to expiry, do not renew, re-let or redevelop at residual
options.mechanics: Keep collecting NNN rent through the existing term, then take the building back in 2030-2035 and either re-let to a new operator or redevelop the site.
pros: Maximises contractual income years collected with no sale friction and no transfer tax, no ULA, no Prop 13 reset.
Preserves the low Prop 13 base-year value (S20) for the whole hold.
Keeps the land and the upside of a re-tenanting or redevelopment in a dense urban core (city density 8,304 persons/sq mi, S05).
cons: You own a declining-WALT asset every year (R03) and cannot sell without taking that discount later, probably deeper.
Full exposure to R01/R11 (tenant credit) with no sale to escape it.
At expiry you inherit vacancy, tenant-improvement cost, leasing commissions and downtime, and you must fund them yourself.
Dense-core Los Angeles rents depend on a restaurant operator that can carry $20/hr+ labour (S19).
options.best_if: You believe the land value alone exceeds the leased-fee value and you can fund a re-letting.

options.name: Negotiate a long renewal first, then sell the re-rated asset (recommended)
options.mechanics: Approach the tenant now for a 10-year extension (plus options) with CPI escalations and a corporate or franchisee guaranty; once executed and documented, sell on the lengthened term in 2027-2029, or hold the re-rated asset if pricing does not cooperate.
pros: Directly attacks R03: a 10-year extension typically re-rates a single-tenant asset from a 'short-term' to a 'financeable' cap rate, which is the single largest value lever available to you.
You keep the sell option the whole time: if the extension is signed and the market pays up, you sell a better asset; if not, you simply do not list it.
Because you are not forced to sell, you are not exposed to R10 (credit seizure) inside a fixed window.
Preserves optionality on the tax side: you can still 1031 later (S24) or hold for a step-up in basis.
Costs you only negotiation time and legal fees; no transfer tax, no ULA, no listing risk until you choose.
cons: You must accept whatever renewal rent the market bears; a tenant with leverage may ask for a rent reduction, TI, or a co-tenancy/termination right.
The negotiated term is a documented asset only if the lease amendment is properly executed and the guaranty is real.
You carry R01/R11 through the negotiation period.
An extension can convert a favourable below-market base into a market-rent reset for property tax if the county treats improvements/new construction as reassessable (S20).
options.best_if: The tenant wants to stay (a 30+ year operating location usually does) — verify before deciding.

recommendation.statement: Pursue a long-term renewal first, then decide whether to sell the re-rated asset or hold. Sell only after the extension is executed (or, if the tenant refuses a renewal on acceptable terms, sell into the current liquid market rather than holding to expiry).
why: The dominant, known, controllable loss is lease-term decay (R03) — it is the only risk on the list that a renewal both removes and monetises.
The dominant uncontrollable risk is cap-rate expansion (R02); a renewal does not remove it, but it makes the asset eligible for the deepest buyer pool, so you are paid for waiting.
Selling now (OPT-A) crystallises the shortest WALT of the hold and pays 4.45% transfer tax plus a Prop 13 reset to do it.
Holding to expiry without renewing (OPT-B) is the highest-variance path: it keeps tenant-credit risk to the end and then hands you vacancy and re-letting cost.
conditions_that_flip_the_answer: Tenant refuses a renewal above X rent → sell now (OPT-A).
Tenant refuses any renewal at all → sell now; do not hold to expiry.
You need cash within 12 months → sell now and start the 1031 identification immediately.
A recession or credit event is clearly underway → do not list; hold OPT-C, because you are not forced to sell.
recommendation.wealth_preservation_balance: OPT-C keeps the asset in a low-risk, income-producing state while preserving an exit at a higher price. It converts an irreversible decision (sell now at the shortest WALT) into a reversible one (renew, then choose). That is the definition of preserving wealth with optionality.

stress_scenarios.name: Base case: rates flat, rent escalates at CPI
stress_scenarios.inputs: Cap rate held at the observed Los Angeles band midpoint (S28-S31); rent escalates with CPI (S07).
stress_scenarios.conclusion: Renewal adds value; selling after renewal captures both the extra term and the escalation.

stress_scenarios.name: Rates +150 bp: cap rate expansion
stress_scenarios.inputs: 10-year Treasury sustained at the 2026 high end (S09), Baa widening (S10).
stress_scenarios.conclusion: Asset value falls even with a renewal. This argues for speed rather than delay once a renewal is signed.

stress_scenarios.name: Tenant stress: store-level closure before expiry
stress_scenarios.inputs: Chain-level losses (S16) propagate to a franchisee failure.
stress_scenarios.conclusion: Value collapses toward land value; security deposit, guaranty and a diversified tenant base are the only protections.

stress_scenarios.name: Credit seizure: exit window closes
stress_scenarios.inputs: CRE delinquency reverts toward its 2010 path (S11).
stress_scenarios.conclusion: You cannot sell. Being unforced — i.e. holding a renewed asset — is the difference between a bad year and a forced sale.

stress_scenarios.name: Local shock: wildfire/earthquake event in the county
stress_scenarios.conclusion: Insurance cost and availability, not the building, become the binding constraint; confirm coverage before renewal.
